transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Um... well, I'm having some trouble at work. I work in meat processing, and... I just keep messing up the paperwork and the cleaning steps. Like, I'll start the sanitation process, or the batch logs, or the end-of-line stuff, and then... I just somehow leave out the last parts. Even though I know I have to finish them right to keep my job. It just... happens.

When you're doing these tasks at work and you leave out the last parts, do you notice any urge or compulsion pushing you to stop, or does it feel more like your mind just goes blank and you lose focus?

I don't really feel an urge to stop. It's more like... I just lose it. Like, I'll start my shift trying really hard to pay attention. But after a while, all the cutting and weighing and checking the labels... it just sort of blurs together. And then I'll realize I've just been staring at the same tray, or the log sheet, and I don't even know what I'm supposed to do next.

When you're staring at the tray or log sheet and lose track of what you're supposed to do next, do you feel like time has passed without you being aware of it, or does it feel more like your mind just won't focus no matter how hard you try?
I guess... it's just hard to focus. Even when I'm trying. I don't know about the time passing part. It's just... I can't keep my mind on it.
When you lose focus like that during your shift, does it happen suddenly - like you snap out of it and realize you've been staring - or does it build up gradually as you get more and more tired?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't... I haven't really paid attention to how it starts. I just kind of realize I'm not doing what I should be. I don't know if it's sudden or... or if it builds up.
Have you ever had someone tell you that you were doing something, or that time passed, when you have no memory of it at all — like a blank spot in your day?
No, I... I don't think so. Not like a blank spot. I just... I'm just not paying attention. Nobody's ever said anything like that to me.
Have you always had trouble focusing and paying attention, even back in school or as a kid? Or did this problem start more recently?

Um... yeah, I guess it's always been an issue. Even back in elementary school. My mom actually still has some of my old report cards from around fourth grade... they usually said I was bright, but that I needed constant reminders to finish my classwork. Or to turn in my homework. 

I remember... I understood the lessons fine. I just... I'd miss chunks of the instructions if the teacher wasn't standing right next to me. So... yeah. It's not a new thing.

When you're at work or trying to focus on something, do you feel like you need to move around, fidget with things, or do you find it hard to sit still? Or is it mainly just the attention part that's the problem?
Um... no, not really. I don't... I don't think I have a hard time staying still. It's mostly just... just the attention part, I guess. I don't really feel the need to move around or anything.
